## Reusable prerequisite: Marcinkiewicz interpolation theorem (`DiscreteSW/Auto/MarcinkiewiczInterpolation.lean`)

Justification: needed for Lemma 2.3 and all its uses (L2.4, L4.2, L5.3, L7.6, C8.2, L9.2, L11.1); Mathlib v4.35.0-rc3 has no weak-type spaces or real interpolation (only the layer-cake formula); it is the named textbook Marcinkiewicz theorem (Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, Thm 1.3.2); formulated for sublinear operators between arbitrary σ-finite measure spaces with normed-group values, weak endpoints `1 ≤ a < b ≤ ∞`, explicit constant.

## Reusable prerequisite: Hardy–Littlewood maximal theorem (`DiscreteSW/Auto/HardyLittlewoodMaximal.lean`)

Justification: needed for Lemma 2.4 and its many uses (C4.4, L5.3, L9.4, L10.1, L11.1, T11.3); Mathlib v4.35.0-rc3 has Vitali covering lemmas but no maximal function theorem; it is the named textbook Hardy–Littlewood maximal theorem (Stein, Singular Integrals, Ch. I §1; Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, Thm 2.1.6); formulated for the centered closed-ball maximal function on a metric measure space with a doubling condition, which covers sup-norm cubes on `Fin n → ℝ` (Lebesgue) and on `Fin n → ℤ` (counting measure).

## Reusable prerequisite: Khintchine inequality and Marcinkiewicz–Zygmund extension (`DiscreteSW/Auto/KhintchineInequality.lean`)

Justification: needed for Lemma 2.6 and its uses (L7.2, T7.7, L9.3); Mathlib v4.35.0-rc3 has no Khintchine inequality; it is the named textbook Khintchine inequality with its standard corollary, the Marcinkiewicz–Zygmund ℓ²-valued extension of bounded linear operators (Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, 3rd ed., Appendix C and §5.5); formulated for finitely many vectors in a real or complex inner product space with uniform random signs, and for linear operators between arbitrary σ-finite measure spaces.

## Reusable prerequisite: Calderón–Zygmund theorem for convolution kernels (`DiscreteSW/Auto/CalderonZygmund.lean`)

Justification: needed for Lemma 4.2 and its uses (L4.3, L4.5, and through them §10); Mathlib v4.35.0-rc3 has no Calderón–Zygmund decomposition or singular-integral bounds; it is the named textbook Calderón–Zygmund theorem (Stein, Singular Integrals, Ch. II §2; Grafakos, Classical Fourier Analysis, 3rd ed., §5.3); formulated for integrable kernels on `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)` with size, gradient and `L²` bounds, constants independent of `‖H‖₁`, for all inputs in `L¹` (weak type) and `L^p`, `1<p<∞`.
